script: My brother said racial slurs, I made him walk home—this changed everything.. I was driving him home after his haircut and PT session, just doing my thing on my day off while the parents were busy. We were joking, throwing insults at each other like any siblings do. Then he drops a line that makes my brain hit a wall: "shut the fuck up, n‑word." I am like, bruh, what? He tries to explain it away, saying he's used it with his Black friends and it's fine because he looks Latino. I tell him that doesn't change the fact it's a slur. He flips it, comparing it to the c‑word, because we live in a mostly Asian area. It's like he's saying the same thing over and over, but he's justifying it. We're both the "golden kids" on my dad's side. I got into a top university last year, so the pressure shifted to him. He's an athlete with D1 potential, but the season's been rough. Dad's frustrated because he's not putting in the effort for recruiting. I've been pushing him to study for the SAT and get back in touch with recruiters, but he says I am controlling. He says I am "naturally smart" and can't understand real hard work. It's like he's dismissing all the effort I've put in, but it's also the most vulnerable conversation we've ever had. I can't forget the slur. About a quarter mile from the house, I pull over and say, "You can walk." He looks shocked. We sit there for ten minutes, and then he gets up, walks away, and repeats the n‑word ten more times. He's 5'10", athletic, and can walk home safely. I get home and tell dad everything while he calls mom. Mom calls me in a frenzy, I explain what he said, but she doesn't seem to care. Dad says he doesn't blame me for making him walk. Mom's pissed, saying I waited until after a vulnerable talk to do this. She wants to take my car and make me quit my job. My brother says I blindsided him. Dad thinks I am right but won't punish him. So, am I the asshole?
